Cause: The OSPF hello interval doesn't match on the r2–r3 link. r2's eth2 is set to 5 seconds and r3's eth1 uses the default 10, so the two routers never form an adjacency. r1 therefore never learns 3.3.3.3/32.

Evidence:
- r1's routing table has no 3.3.3.3/32. It does have 10.0.0.4/30 via r2, because r2 advertises that connected link.
- r2's only OSPF neighbor is r1 (Full). r3 has no OSPF neighbors at all.
- r2's running config for `interface eth2` (to-r3) has `ip ospf hello-interval 5`.
- r3's running config for `interface eth1` (to-r2) has no hello-interval, so it uses the default of 10 seconds.
- Both ends have `ip ospf network point-to-point` and are in area 0, with correct addresses on 10.0.0.4/30 (10.0.0.5 and 10.0.0.6). The hello timer is the only difference I found.
- I inferred the mismatch from the configs. I didn't check the timers with a live interface command or ping.

Suggested fix: Make the hello interval the same on both ends of the link. Either remove `ip ospf hello-interval 5` from r2 eth2, or add `ip ospf hello-interval 5` to r3 eth1. Also keep the dead interval matching, since it is derived from the hello interval unless set explicitly. After that, check that the r2–r3 adjacency reaches Full and that r1 has a route to 3.3.3.3.
